memory_candidates.content: In agent-system's runtime-file-patterns.sh, gitignore patterns are **/-prefixed shell globs (e.g. **/.orchestrator-multi-state*.json), which use bash pathname-expansion semantics (* = zero-or-more of any char) rather than requiring a literal separator. This means a single canonical pattern can already tolerate multiple historical naming-generation variants (un-suffixed, hyphen-suffixed, dot-separator, .prev- variant) with zero changes -- the actual coverage gap was in a downstream consumer (reap-session-runtime-files.sh) that used a narrower literal bash-array glob requiring a literal hyphen. When auditing 'does X cover Y' for a glob-based ignore/allow list, check the glob semantics before assuming a gap exists in the canonical pattern itself.

check-runtime-file-tracking.sh's Check B (no ephemeral-class file is tracked) only scans the 18 canonical members of runtime-file-patterns.sh's RUNTIME_FILE_B_REGEX array. A file from a fully retired/superseded naming convention that was never added to that array (e.g. a 'meta-return' return-file convention retired from skill-meta before this check existed) can be currently git-tracked and committed at HEAD while the check reports a clean PASS. Verification tooling built around 'the canonical N-member list' is only as complete as that list -- a dead convention's stray tracked file is invisible to it by construction, not merely by bug.

skill-refresh/SKILL.md's Steps 4.5 (reap-session-runtime-files.sh) and 4.6 (task-lock.sh session-reap) are a directly portable reference for wiring the same two non-interactive, threshold-gated reap calls into any other skill (e.g. skill-todo): both echo the reaper's own output verbatim, both reuse a single dry_run boolean parsed once in Step 1, and both are called unconditionally (no AskUserQuestion gate) since they are pure age-threshold sweeps, not user-judgment decisions.
